question: While I welcome the recognition of tourism as a major economic pillar (10 % of Gross Added Value, 20 million jobs), the Commission’s new strategy widens the gap between east and west. It introduces new bureaucratic burdens without dedicated funding, prioritises the issue of overtourism in western metropolises at the expense of underpromoted regions, and ignores transport infrastructure disparities in central and eastern Europe. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Why is it refusing to establish a dedicated budget line for tourism in the next multiannual financial framework, preferring the allocation of funds to mainstream programmes that are difficult for SMEs in eastern countries to access?
How will it adjust the balanced tourism toolkit to avoid restricting emerging destinations in central and eastern Europe, whose objective is to increase tourism flows?

What objective criteria will be used to ensure that Destination Europe funds actively promote untapped attractions in Romania and the wider region, avoiding budgets focusing on established destinations in western Europe?
